title: mistri app manifest
description: A mistri App: identity (id, name); data (connection, sources, resources); auth; content (views, pages, home, nav); and chrome (ui). The parsers in src/shared/app*.ts are the truth; this schema is the authoring aid, kept honest by test/schema.test.ts.

id.description: Absent, it derives from the name.

name.description: An app is named after what it is for.

connection.description: The one connection this App is for, by id or name. Absent means every connection. Not with sources. A name that is an identifier is also the App's one source's: commands name it in defineSource.

sources.description: Named connection bindings. At most one says default: true; several may share a connection, each with its own schema. Not with root connection.

resources.description: One block per logical resource, keyed bare for the default source or source.name for a secondary one.

unions.description: Read-only resources over tables that share a shape, each listed in one order and one page: union('my_requests', [{ from: 'incident', as: { title: 'short_description' } }, …]). Each branch is read under the reader's own grants and row policy; a row's from and key open its own record.

from.description: The branch's resource.

as.description: The union's column → this resource's own column. Every branch names the same union columns.

track.description: What the App's commands keep unless one says otherwise: none, receipts (a retried request is answered once) or audit (the receipt and every change). A door that retries (the App API, MCP, a job) keeps at least receipts.

live.description: Whether the App's open pages follow other people's changes (live sync): a list, a record and a dashboard read again what a change touched, as it commits. Off unless true; then pages refresh on focus and after their own saves, and a dashboard reads every section again each minute while shown. The operator's --no-live wins. A resource leaves it with live: false.

branding.description: What each tenant may change about how the App looks to its people, and which tenant roles may save it. Never the grounds, the ink or the recipes. A tenant App only.

allow.description: What each tenant may set. preset (which of themes it starts from) needs more than one of themes; locale is the tenant's language, under each person's own.

editors.description: The tenant roles whose members may save it: a tenant's admins.

themes.description: The themes a tenant starts from (defineTheme results or built-in names); the first is the default. Absent: the App's own look.

views.description: Everything a visitor can open, keyed: the key is the view’s address.

pages.description: Record pages keyed by id, or one file per page under pages/ (its basename the key).

features.description: Ordered slices of content merged at load, every merge checked: views, pages, a nav fragment the App places with { feature }, how resources present, home rules appended after the App's, and grants to the App's roles within its ceilings. Identical facts merge; conflicting ones are refused, naming both contributors.

home.description: Where a visitor starts, required: a view id for everyone, or rules read in order that end with a rule with no condition.

nav.description: Arrangement only: view ids, { to, label }, and groups, in order. Optional: an App without nav has no menu.

duration.description: A whole number and a unit: '30 seconds', '5 minutes', '12 hours', '3 days', '2 weeks'.

audience.description: Who an audience holds: every condition given must hold. allow and deny name account ids and decide first.

retention.description: How long the runtime keeps what it writes about the App as it runs; a daily job forgets what is older. history: who changed which record (default 730 days). commands: the command journal's receipts, audit and events (default 730 days). attempts: the finished tries of jobs and webhook deliveries; one still pending or waiting for a redrive is never forgotten (default 30 days). Each is a duration, or 'forever' to keep it all.

retentionSpan.description: A duration above zero ('30 days', '12 weeks') or 'forever'.

assistant.description: The in-App assistant: it reads as the signed-in person under their grants, and every write it proposes waits for the person to confirm it. The model key is the operator's (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY). On a tenant App it answers only for the tenants the platform owner turns it on for.

instructions.description: What it is for and how it answers, appended to the platform's own rules.

starters.description: Questions an empty conversation offers, each sent as the person's own when pressed: a line alone everywhere, { text, views, records } only in those views' rooms or on a record of those tables. At most six in one place.

views.description: View keys: offered while one of these views is the room.

records.description: Table names: offered while a record of one of these tables is open. Needs the record placement.

model.description: The model id; claude-sonnet-5-5 when absent.

roles.description: The roles offered it; absent, everyone who may open the App.

exclude.description: Verbs it may never propose: resource.action, or resource.new for the New form.

placement.description: panel beside every room; record takes the open record as context; page gives it a room at /{app}/assistant. Absent, panel and record.

analytics.description: Behavior analytics, off unless declared: the built-in kinds collected, the custom events components may emit, and funnels read over them. Where events are stored is configuration (`analytics.store`), not the App's.

collect.description: Built-in kinds recorded: a view or page opening by its id, a command's outcome at admission, a form step reached and its submit.

events.description: Custom events a component emits through useAnalytics().emit, each with the only fields it may carry.

funnels.description: Ordered steps a unit passes within a conversion window, counted over the stored events.

appSwitcher.description: Explicit authored App choices only. Omission means no switcher. Group labels and link labels within each group must be unique after trimming and case folding (checked by the parser).

importDecl.description: Rows from a CSV file. true imports them as new records through the ordinary insert, under the reader's grants and the resource's validation. An object runs 'command' once per row, on the record its 'match' columns find.

match.description: The resource's own columns that find the record each row runs on; a reference column is found by the record's name.

apiRead.description: Exposure metadata; it opens no routes by itself. Commands must be targeted and are served only beside their --commands registry. Runtime checks logical catalog, roles, the command registry and authority lock.

apiEvents.description: Command events the event feed serves, each its own token operation (event:<name>).

apiDraft.description: Full draft vocabulary; active App roots currently accept only the read subset. Runtime checks declared roles, field subsets, reserved names and duplicate logical references.

publicSpec.description: Serve the OpenAPI document at …/$openapi without a token: every operation the API declares, without its roles or standing queries. Absent or false, the document is a token's own, narrowed to what it may do.

network.description: Let the API and its MCP endpoint answer beyond loopback when the server listens there (--host, --allowed-host, --trust-proxy). Absent, they answer loopback only and a wider listener refuses to start. Recorded in authority.lock.

formField.description: A local column name; relationship paths and expressions are unavailable. Checked against the actual catalog.

formText.description: Static plain text. No row-value interpolation.

autoValue.description: A value filled in rather than stated: the constants today, now and me from @mistriwork/mistri/app. today is the day, on a date column; now the moment; me the signed-in person (their row on a reference to the auth.me table, their email on a text column). A form and a fixed action's set fill in all three.

formScalar.description: Values normalize using actual column metadata. Use strings for exact decimals and large integers; unsafe numeric literals are refused.

formCondition.description: A condition in the query language, the one a page section's or an action's when speaks: "completed = false", "stage = closed_won and probability < 100", "pay_type in (salary, hourly)", "due_on is empty". Read against the record's own values: local columns compared with =, !=, <, <=, >, >=, in and is (not) empty, joined by and, or and parentheses; no paths, no text matching, at most 16 comparisons. Unknown or uncomparable dependencies stay unresolved. Text and booleans support only = and !=; ordered comparisons require compatible numeric or temporal columns.

formRowFieldList.description: The fields in order. An inner list is a row, drawn side by side (one column on a narrow form): [["email", "phone"], "company"]. At most 3 to a row; each field once.

formGroups.description: Semantic presentation groups. The App checker also rejects duplicate members across groups and members excluded by show or read access. Ungrouped shown fields remain shown. Groups never grant access.

savedFormSteps.description: A saved form's steps: each asks its own command's inputs, and its handler saves them.

id.description: Unique within the form. Absent, the label's slug, as step() makes it.

title.description: The intake style's heading for the step; absent, the label.

next.description: The primary button's words on this step; absent, Continue.

formSteps.description: Finite presentation steps. When show is omitted, the steps select the fields in step order. Every field is owned by exactly one step; steps never grant access or execute hooks.

id.description: Unique within the form. Absent, the label's slug, as step() makes it.

fields.description: The fields in order. An inner list is a row, drawn side by side: [["first_name", "last_name"], "dob"]. At most 3 to a row.

title.description: The intake style's heading for the step; absent, the label.

next.description: The primary button's words on this step; absent, Continue.

skip.description: The primary's words while every field of the step is empty.

href.description: https://, mailto: or tel: only — never a relative path, http:, javascript: or data:. Checked at load.

commandGrants.description: Explicit server command identifiers only. No wildcard grants or implied CRUD access.

formRule.description: The record must meet `must`, a condition in the query language, wherever `when` holds: "close_date >= created_on" (beside a number, date or flag a bare word naming a column compares with it), "name is not empty" (blank text is empty), "order_id.status = bench" (through one reference, the record it names, judged on the server). The message is shown at the first column `must` names, or the reference a path reads through. Evaluated after trusted default resolution or update merging; an unknown condition cannot disable a rule.

formVisibility.description: Each field shown only while the draft matches its condition. Presentation only. Targets must be shown/readable; condition dependencies must be readable local columns. Hiding a field never weakens authoritative resource validation.

form.description: The New form wherever this resource's records are created from a list: every view's New button and quickAdd.

from.description: One reference of this table, then a column of the table it names: service_id.price.

defaults.description: The values a new record starts with. Besides a literal, three constants: today on a date column, now on a date-and-time column, and me (the signed-in person's row on a reference to the auth.me table, their email on a text column) — { "auto": "today" } and so on in JSON. Filled in as the form opens, and by the server on a create that leaves them out; a column the form does not show is the server's, whatever a create says. The text "today", "now" or "me" is refused, since it would read as the value filled in. Or { "from": "service_id.price" }: the value of the record a reference names, refreshed as it is chosen until the person edits it, and filled by the server where a create leaves it out.

style.description: How the steps are drawn, both under one progress bar: the stepper (default, the step's name over its fields) or the intake style.

description.description: One sentence under the form's heading.

open.description: 'drawer': over the list, which stays in sight. 'page': a centered page in the content pane. Absent: a drawer for up to 8 fields without steps, a page for more or with steps.

lines.description: Child rows asked with the record and inserted with it in one transaction, each collection a grid of inputs: { label: 'Lines', from: 'order_line', whose: 'order_id', show: ['product_id', 'quantity'], order: 'position' }.

from.description: The child resource; the App writes it.

whose.description: The child's reference to the new record, filled by the server.

show.description: The child's columns each row asks, as inputs; not whose or order.

order.description: A numeric column the rows' places fill, 1, 2, 3 …

min.description: Fewest rows the record is saved with.

live.description: The resource's computed columns and rollups the form says as it is filled in, worked out by the server's own evaluator. A preview: the saved record's figures are the server's.

fields.description: Each shown field's own dress on this form: caption, help, placeholder, lines and, for a reference, the choices it narrows to.

formFieldDress.description: One field of a resource's New form. The input is chosen from the column: a vocabulary is radios (up to four words) or a listbox in its display words, a flag a switch, a date and a date-and-time pickers, money carries its currency, long or prose-named text is several lines.

multiline.description: A text column: true draws several lines, false one, whatever its type says.

as.description: A vocabulary or a flag drawn as icon-less cards, a row of buttons, radios or a listbox, over the default its size and kind pick. A flag is buttons or select.

where.description: A reference: offer only the records whose column (the key) equals this form's field (the value): { project_id: 'project_id' }. Enforced on every write.

actions.description: What may be done to one record, keyed by its id and drawn in the order written: defined once and offered wherever the records appear — on record pages, in a queue (the bulk ones, for a selection), on a board (updates that set exactly its by). A header's primary and destructive, a queue's actions and a role's actions name one by its id.

set.description: Column → value the action writes: a literal, or a value the server works out in the write — { "auto": "now" } (the constant now: a DATE gets the day in ui.timezone, else UTC; a TIMESTAMP or DATETIME with no zone the wall clock in ui.timezone (UTC without one), one with a zone (timestamptz) the UTC instant), { "auto": "today" } (the App's day, into a DATE), { "auto": "me" } (the constant me: the signed-in account's email, into a text column of an App with auth), or a constant expression in the computed-column grammar, { "type": "date", "value": "today + 14 days" } (computed.date('today + 14 days')), which reads no column and fits its column's type. The text "now", "today" or "me", and text starting with "=", is refused, since it would read as one of those.

value.description: A constant expression: numbers, true, false, today, now, me, comparisons, and, or, not, + - * /, and date spans (today + 14 days, now + 1 week). No column.

when.description: Shown only when the record matches, in the query language.

confirm.description: Ask before writing. A command that asks nothing runs on one click unless it confirms; a command with inputs asks them in its form, which is its confirmation, and is refused one.

reason.description: A column this action asks a reason for and writes with its set. Required when the action runs; not with bulk or a command.

bulk.description: May run on a selection, App-wide: a queue offers it for its selection. A fixed update is one ordinary write per selected record, with results per record; a command must declare targets: many and runs the whole selection as one atomic request.

header.description: false keeps the button out of the record's action bar and its menu, for a verb the App runs from its own place: a custom component through useCommand, a queue's selection, a board's lane. Still granted, judged and run as before; a record header that names it is refused.

inputs.description: A command action's input drawn by the App's own input component (kind 'input'), in its form. An input in a group is named by its path (trade.vin), and in a repeating group stands in every row.

format.description: money: currency formatting (metrics compact to "$27.9M"). percent: the value is 0–100, shown with %. number: separators forced on. relative: a date said from today ("in 3 days", "64 days ago"), the date itself in the tooltip. items: a text of one item per line, drawn as a list (a line of them where there is no room). duration: a number of seconds said as its two largest units ("2h 15m"), the seconds in the tooltip. email, phone, url: a value of that shape is a link to write to, call or open; an App links a column named like one without a rule. richText: sanitized HTML, drawn formatted on a record and as an excerpt in a list, edited in the rich text editor; the server sanitizes every write and reads Markdown into it. avatars: the people on a thing (an array, a JSON array, or one name per line or comma) as up to three overlapping initials discs and a "+N"; takes nothing else. rating: a whole number of stars out of outOf (5). color: a hex color as its swatch and code. time, month, year: a time of day, a month, a year in the reader's words, each edited in its native picker. json: a JSON document as a tree, edited as text whose problem is said while it is typed; the server refuses a write that is not JSON. qr: the value as a QR code to scan. These draw the value their own way.

face.description: The face this column's values are set in, over the look's own: data (the look's data face, usually monospace), ui (the interface's reading face) or code (always monospace, for a VIN or a hash). Left out, an App sets a key, a reference, a code or a QR value in the data face and any other text in the reading face. A rule with a component takes no face, the component sets its own; masked: true takes none either.

outOf.description: With format rating: the stars of its scale (5 when unsaid).

ring.description: With format percent: the value as a small ring filled against 100.

slider.description: A number edited by dragging along its range, the figure beside it: { min: 0, max: 10 }.

scan.description: A code typed or read by the camera where the browser can read codes; takes no format.

signature.description: On a column that points at a file resource: a signature drawn or typed, kept as a PNG row of it and drawn as the picture; takes no format.

icon.description: A small tinted square before the value in a list's cell: an App icon, or { mark, toneOf } where toneOf names another column of the record whose tone rule tints each row's square.

colors.description: Value → one of the theme's eight chart colors (1–8): the stripe and chip of a board card's category.

labelColumn.description: The column a person is shown by, or a template of the people's own columns ('{first_name} {last_name}'). Typing after the @ matches the start of any word of it, and of the handle where that is text; the handle (by) is what is stored.

groups.description: The teams an @ names as well, each told as its members: their resource, handle and shown column, and the resource of link rows that puts a person in a team (absent: the people resource references the team).

mentions.description: With format richText: who an @ names — the resource of people, the column stored as the handle, the column shown or a template of their columns ('{first_name} {last_name}') — and the teams an @ may name as well.

images.description: With format richText: the file resource a pasted or dropped picture is kept in, as an attachment of the record.

masked.description: true: a short placeholder is drawn instead of every value, everywhere, the record's name included, and the rule takes nothing else. { prefix: 'ENC:' }: only the values that start with it, said as the prefix and a placeholder; any other value is drawn by the rest of the rule. Presentation, not protection: the value still reaches the browser; use hidden to keep a column out of it.

currency.description: ISO 4217, for "money"; defaults to the App's currency, then USD. { column: 'currency_code' }: each row's own code, read from that text column of the resource.

minor.description: With "money": the integer column holds minor units (cents), said and edited in the currency's own decimals — 1999 is $19.99, ¥1,999, 1.999 KWD.

unit.description: With "number", "money" or no format on a numeric column: the unit said after the figure — "mi", "kg", "/mo" (a leading slash joins without a space: "$242/mo").

tone.description: Value → tone pills. Keys may be exact values, or numeric thresholds like ">= 90" — for numbers, the first satisfied threshold (in written order) wins. The key "*" is the fallback; values it does not name wear neutral.

bar.description: Draw the value as a small bar: true on format "percent", which fills against 100; for any other number, the value that fills it (bar: 5 for a rating out of five). A tone rule colors the bar.

avatar.description: An initials disc before the value: a person's or a company's name. Given a file resource ({ from, whose, sort? }), the disc is the record's photo, drawn through the file route under the reader's grants, and the initials where there is none.

from.description: A resource whose rows are files.

whose.description: Its column that points at the record the avatar is of.

icons.description: Value → an App icon drawn before the word (priority as signal bars, a status's mark), where a tone's dot would stand and in its color; the word stays.

values.description: The words a vocabulary's values are said as: a map of stored value to word ({ "PUB": "Published" }); any value it does not name is still said as words, as are the values of a column with a tone (IN_REVIEW reads "In review"). The stored value still sorts, filters and keys tone and icons.

subtitle.description: Another column of the same record, said as a muted second line under the value in lists.

component.description: A value renderer (kind 'value'): the App draws the value with it; sort, filter, totals and export keep the raw value.

roleFieldGrant.description: A role's columns of one resource. read omitted is the resource's own read ceiling, so a role may narrow only write.

column.description: The balance: a reference of this resource, then a number column of the record it names ("part_id.on_hand").

by.description: This row's number column holding how much it uses; one each when absent.

message.description: What a refusal says, {path} read from the record the balance is on: "Only {part_id.on_hand} of {part_id.name} left". A message of the App's catalogs (msg('stock.short', { left: 'part_id.on_hand' })) binds each place to its path and is said in the reader's language.

floor.description: false lets the balance go below zero.

resource.description: One logical resource and everything the App says about it: binding, ceiling, columns, display, validation, captions, New form, actions, default page and what a record is called.

noun.description: What one record is called, as it reads mid-sentence ("issue"; its plural by rule), or { one, many } for a plural no rule makes. It names New, a split's detail and, when they say none, a page and a list.

physical.description: The physical table id when it is not inferred. The only place an engine-schema-qualified id ("public.opportunity") appears.

access.description: The App's ceiling for this resource. An App serves only its declared resources, and a declared one reads; say 'write' for one the App writes. With auth.roles, roles grant within the ceilings.

delete.description: Opt-in: records of this resource can be deleted (Delete, last in the record's More menu). Absent, the server refuses deletes. It needs access 'write'.

favorite.description: Opt-in: a star on the records, so a reader can keep them in Favorites.

settings.description: A settings record: the resource holds one row (a company profile, payroll settings), opened from the reader's settings (the account menu) under these words. Its page and grants are the resource's own; the first row by key is the one opened.

file.description: The rows are files: content names the binary column holding the bytes (BLOB, bytea), name the file name; type and size, when named, are filled from the upload; thumbnail names a smaller copy for cards. A related list over the resource draws as attachments, uploading where the reader may add a row (its create names the label). maxBytes caps an upload (10 MB when unsaid, at most 25 MB). In a row-policy App an upload is an insert the policy judges, and removing a file a delete. A tenant App reads and uploads its files on the tenant's lease, each at most 10 MB, and only its own tenant's. storage 'bucket' keeps new files' bytes in an S3-compatible bucket (AWS S3, R2, MinIO, B2, Tigris), the row naming the object in its object column; the server's MISTRI_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID and MISTRI_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY sign every request, and the server does not start without them. object and hash need no grant: a reader of content reads the file, and they are the server's alone, sent to no browser and named by no request, App API or MCP tool. An upload is one request, so maxBytes stays at most 25 MB with a bucket; multipart upload is not supported. mistri migrate files moves files to where storage says and sweeps objects no row names; an App served with jobs is swept daily by the server, a tenant App tenant by tenant.

thumbnail.description: A binary column holding a smaller copy of each file's picture, which cards and gallery strips draw instead of the whole file. Whoever writes the row fills it (a seed, an import); a row without one is drawn from the file itself.

object.description: A text column naming each file's object in the bucket; null for a file kept in content. The server's alone: granted with content, named by no request.

hash.description: A text column the upload fills with the file's SHA-256 (hex), which tags it for caches. The server's alone: granted with content, named by no request.

storage.description: Where new files' bytes go: database (when unsaid) or bucket. A file is read from wherever its row says.

bucket.description: An S3-compatible bucket the files' bytes are kept in: its address only, the credentials being the server's environment.

region.description: Its region: us-east-1 when unsaid; auto for R2.

endpoint.description: The service's address, for any but AWS: https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com, or a local one such as `http://localhost:9000`.

pathStyle.description: true addresses the bucket as a path (<endpoint>/<name>/<key>), as MinIO wants; otherwise as a host.

prefix.description: A folder every key goes under, so Apps can share one bucket.

presign.description: true sends a download straight from the bucket, by a redirect to a URL signed for a minute; otherwise it passes through the server.

tags.description: The records carry tags: rows of to, linked through a table with one reference to this resource and one to to. They draw as chips under the record's title; where through is declared writable with delete: true, a picker adds and removes them one link row at a time. toneOf names a column of to holding good, warn, bad, info or neutral.

search.description: Search through a search provider: fields are the columns the index holds, or one step along a reference (requester.name) whose value each document copies and follows; connection names the provider's connection. The list's filter box, reference pickers and the palette ask it and re-read the rows under the reader's grants; while it is down they search the database. Needs a single-column primary key. On a tenant App each document keeps its tenant and a search asks within the member's tenant. Search providers are packs (Typesense is @mistriwork/search-typesense), which ship after 1.0; until one is plugged in, an App that declares search is refused at startup.

fields.description: Column ceiling for signed-in roles: needs auth with auth.roles; write needs access 'write'. To keep a column from every reader, use hidden.

hidden.description: Columns no reader of the App is ever served, with sign-in or without. Cut from the catalog the server answers with; never the primary key, the address or a search field.

references.description: Soft keys: column -> { to, column? }, a column naming a record of another resource without a database foreign key. The target column (default its primary key) must be proven unique. Joined within one connection; into a source on another connection, read in two steps (labels, links, related lists; no filter or sort through it). Never authority for a write.

types.description: SQLite: a TEXT column → "date" or "datetime" when it holds ISO dates, so windows, timelines, calendars, date presets and date filters take it. The database still holds text.

display.description: How each column’s values dress, keyed by column.

validation.description: Resource invariants, enforced on every write, independent of views and forms.

text.description: How long a text column's value may be and what form it takes, keyed by column: min and max characters and a pattern the whole value matches, with an optional message. The New form says the rule as someone types; the server holds every write to it. On PostgreSQL a varchar(n) and a simple char_length or ~ CHECK give the database's rule free; the App's wins key by key.

pattern.description: A JavaScript regular expression the whole value matches.

message.description: What the form says when the rule is not met.

labels.description: One caption per column or label path: literal text, or a message of the App's catalogs (msg('lead.title')) said in each reader's language.

recordLabel.description: What names one record: a column or path, or a template of them in braces ('PO-{id}', '{product_id.name} x {qty}'), computed in the statement; or a message of the App's catalogs whose arguments are those columns. A table with no name column of its own is named by its noun and key unless this says otherwise.

when.description: Query-language conditions over the record's own columns the record must meet then: "status = 'open'".

at.description: Timers at an instant the record keeps: a date or timestamp column, and the command run through the jobs once its time has passed and the record matches when, once for each instant the column holds; a new time arms it again.

page.description: The page this resource's records open through, only when two pages share its base.

owner.description: Who owns the resource's rows under auth.rows 'tenant', where it is required: one tenant's (by its ownership column), shared global data, or the platform realm's.

clone.description: What a tenant clone copies of this tenant-owned resource into a sandbox tenant: 'config' rows always, 'sample' rows only when the clone asks for samples. Unmarked resources are never copied. Startup refuses a marked resource whose key or references a clone cannot remap.

live.description: false: on an App with live: true, a write to this table is not announced and no page follows it (a hot or log-like table); its pages refresh on focus and after their own saves. Absent, the App's choice. Means nothing on an App without live: true.

redact.description: Columns the support write trail records as a keyed hash instead of their value, or 'values' for every column.

audit.description: What the durable support write trail keeps of these rows.

computed.description: Virtual columns, each a typed expression over the record's own columns in the query language's words, with today, now and me: { is_overdue: { type: 'boolean', value: 'due_on < today and not completed' } }; hours and minutes move an instant (now - 30 minutes, due_at - 2 hours). Written into the statement, read like a column everywhere a column is; never written, never in a form, and served to a role only where every column it reads is.

value.description: The expression: columns and paths through references, numbers, quoted text, true, false, today, now, me, comparisons, and, or, not, in (…), is empty, + - * /, date spans (+ 3 months), and coalesce(a, b, …), round(x) or round(x, places), abs(x), min(a, b, …) and max(a, b, …).

rollups.description: Numbers about the rows that point at each record, by name, read like columns wherever a column is (a list's show, a sort, a condition, a command's when, a page's fields, display and labels): count(from), sum, min or max (from, column), or latest (from, column), a column of the newest row. Computed in the record's own statement through the child's grants and row scope; never written.

from.description: The resource whose rows point at this one.

column.description: The column of `from` a sum, min, max or latest reads; a count names none. A sum, min or max may read a computed column of `from` that reads only its row's own columns, written inline; a latest reads a stored column of any type, and serves its vocabulary.

sort.description: A latest's order: the column of `from`, a date or a number, whose greatest value is the newest row (its key breaks a tie, and a row without one is never newer than a row with one). Its integer key when absent.

whose.description: The reference on `from` that points here, when there is more than one; or two, `task_id.project_id`, when `from` points at a record that points here.

query.description: Which of `from`'s rows count, in the query language over its own columns, its computed columns that read only its own row, and paths through its references to a stored column: "status = open", "sales_order_id.status != cancelled", "breaching = true". A computed column's `now` and `today` are the request's.

segment.description: One of from's segments: the rows it names are the ones counted, ANDed with query.

segments.description: Named conditions on this resource's rows, each read as one word wherever its table's rows are asked: a tab, a source ("work_order.overdue"), a rollup's segment, a query. One may name another, and only ever narrows; its label is its name said as words unless it gives one.

consumes.description: This row uses up a number on the record it points at, kept true on every write: an insert takes by from the balance (refused below zero), a delete gives it back, an edit moves the difference. One, or a list.

restocks.description: consumes the other way round, on a line that brings stock in (a receipt, a return to stock): an insert adds by to the balance, an edit moves the difference, and a delete takes it back out, refused where what it brought in has been used since. One, or a list.

defined.description: Row-defined fields, keyed by the record's JSON column: { from, per? }. from is the declared resource whose rows (key, label, type, options, required, help, position) define the column's keys; per, a column both tables have, picks the definitions whose value equals the record's, and those whose value is empty. Drawn as the record's own fields, judged at the server, asked by a list as column.key.

from.description: The resource whose rows define the fields.

per.description: A column the record and the definitions both have.

flows.description: Flows whose steps are rows: { from, steps, set?, events?, kinds? }. from and steps are declared resources whose rows are the flows (id, name, start: created | updated | manual, and condition?, changes?, active?) and their steps (flow_id, position, kind, and the columns a kind reads: title, duration, field, value, condition, goto, event, audience, message, and on a kind that waits mode, remind). A notify step tells the audience a notify rule names with on: { flow }. Steps sharing a position start together and join; a run keeps the rows it started with. A jobs module's flowRunner runs them on this resource's records, durably; a step of an App kind runs one of the App's commands on the record.

from.description: The resource whose rows are the flows.

steps.description: The resource whose rows are the flows' steps.

set.description: The record's own columns a set step may write.

events.description: Each event a run may wait for, with the payload field that names the record: { "po.decided": "order" }.

kinds.description: The step kinds the App adds, each running one of its commands on the record.

command.description: The command the step runs on the record.

input.description: Step columns passed to the command under their own names; 'note?' for one a step may leave empty.

waitFor.description: One of events, waited for once the command has run.

remind.description: A command run on the record, with the step's input, each time a step's remind passes without the event; needs waitFor.

notify.description: Which writes tell which people, kept in each person's inbox and written in the triggering write's own transaction, in reserved tables provisioned once (mistri migrate stores up, or provisionStores from @mistriwork/mistri/maintenance with only: ['inbox']). The person who made the write is never told. Needs sign-in; not under auth.rows 'tenant'.

email.description: Email each notice too, after the write commits, through the config's email service: to accounts only, while they may read the record, unless they turned email off.

mentions.description: The people a text column mentions: a plain text column's @handle words by a handle column of the table auth.me names ({ in: 'body', by: 'handle' }), a rich text column's stored mentions (its display rule's by, which this must agree with), a team as its members; an update tells only whom it newly mentions.

on.description: What happens: a new record, any change, a change to one of these columns (an assignment), the action that ran, by its id, or a flow's notify step telling this audience.

when.description: Only when the record, after the write, meets this condition in the query language over its own columns: status = received or status = cancelled. = , != and in, joined by and / or.

to.description: Who is told: a text column holding an email, a reference to the table auth.me names, or a path of at most two references to either.

title.description: The notice, with {column} and {reference.column} filled from the record after the write; a message of the App's catalogs (msg('ticket.assigned', { title: 'title' })) is said in each recipient's own language.

send.description: Tell it on an integration's channel too: the title is the message, sent to the address the record holds after the write commits, unless the recipient opted out, held through the quiet hours. With send, to may be left out.

channel.description: The channel a listed integration provides, like sms.

to.description: The text column holding the address on that channel, or a path of at most two references to one.

consent.description: A column that is true where the App holds the recipient's consent; absent or false, only a recipient who opted in on the channel is told.

timezone.description: A text column holding the recipient's IANA time zone, which the quiet hours are read in.

opens.description: The reference whose record the notice opens; absent, the record itself.

view.description: The list view its records are addressed through (/{app}/{view}/{id}), when more than one lists them: a preference for whoever is served it, passed over for a person who is not. Absent: the first list view over it, among the views that person is served, in the menu's order with no standing query and no split.

address.description: A natural key: the column whose value is the record's address instead of its primary key. mistri check refuses one the catalog does not prove NOT NULL and unique; in a tenant App, unique within the tenant (UNIQUE (tenant_id, number)) is enough.

slug.description: true follows a numeric id with the record's name on public pages (/forecourt/vehicles/1-2021-toyota-corolla). Only the id is read back.

inputs.description: A column's control in the resource's edit and New forms, drawn by the App's own input component (kind 'input').

label.description: The role's name as people read it, wherever a screen names the role (accounts, grants, invitations). Absent: the id, made readable. Words only; it grants nothing.

extends.description: Another role whose grants this one holds too: { manager: { extends: 'mechanic', commands: ['approveQuote'] } }. A chain is followed; a loop is refused. Only grants pass down, each the union of both; never label, claims or service, and only within one realm. A view's or page's roles open to a role that extends one they name; a row policy's principal.roles still match by name.

read.description: true grants the read ceiling (every declared resource); a list names some of them.

write.description: true grants the write ceiling (resources with access 'write'), within the role's reads.

create.description: Of what the role writes, what it makes new records in. Absent: everything it writes. false: it edits and never creates (no New, quick add or related add, and the server refuses the insert). A list names the few it creates.

export.description: Tables the role may export (the whole matching list as a CSV or JSON file) beyond those it writes, which it always may. Of what it reads. A signed-out visitor never may. An App without role grants keeps its one switch, ui.export.

operations.description: Operator reads over the authenticated App host: readiness, bundle (the sanitized support bundle) and workflows (the durable workflows room, with Cancel and Retry). In a suite's Console, for this App only: workflows, jobs (list and redrive), deliveries (event and webhook deliveries, list and redrive), stores (store layout status) and analytics (read-only). With the platform realm, support reads the support sessions of the role's own realm: a tenant role its own tenant's, a platform role every tenant's (the one view naming the operator); never granted by a feature. Independent of data and command grants.

fields.description: Column narrowing per resource, within the resource's own fields. Omit read to narrow only write.

realm.description: The realm the role grants in: a tenant's (the default) or the platform realm's. Required on every role once auth.tenancy.platform is declared; a platform role edits only the platform's own writable resources, never the profile's New, and changes a tenant's rows only through its commands.

provider.description: The one named identity provider whose claims these are, oidc('workforce') or saml('corp'): a sign-in through another never reads the rule. Without it any of the App's providers does, and check warns where there are several.

claims.description: The identity provider's claims that give this role: { <claim, or a dotted path into one>: [values] }, and optionally provider, the one provider they are read from. Re-read at every sign-in; not in a tenant App.

service.description: A role only a service principal holds (a jobs module's principals, an App API token), never a person: a free-form page is offered to it only where the page names it; it is never defaultRole and has no claims.

actionGrants.description: Fixed actions the role runs without write, by resource and action id: { pay_run: ['submit'] }. Each resource is one the role reads, with access 'write', and does not write; each id is one of its fixed (set) actions. The server admits the update only as that action: its set, its reason column, its when on the stored row. Needs auth.rows 'all'.

featureGrant.description: A feature's grant to a role the App declares: resources by name, within the App's ceilings, added to what the App grants. true, the whole ceiling, is the App's to grant.

realm.description: May only restate an identical, explicitly declared root role realm. Cross-contributor agreement is checked by the App checker; a feature cannot introduce a realm.

write.description: Within the role's reads and the App's write ceiling.

operations.description: Operator reads over the authenticated App host: readiness, bundle (the sanitized support bundle) and workflows (the durable workflows room, with Cancel and Retry). In a suite's Console, for this App only: workflows, jobs (list and redrive), deliveries (event and webhook deliveries, list and redrive), stores (store layout status) and analytics (read-only). Independent of data and command grants.

fields.description: Column narrowing per resource, within the resource's own fields. Omit read to narrow only write.

auth.description: Sign-in for this App, through Better Auth. Present, every request needs a session.

anyOf.description: oidc('workforce'): an identity provider the config file names (kind "oidc"). oidc.tenants(): each tenant's own, found by the email's domain, in a tenant App.
saml('okta'): a SAML 2.0 identity provider the config file names (kind "saml"). saml.tenants(): each tenant's own, found by the email's domain, in a tenant App.

providers.description: How people sign in. GitHub and Google read their client id and secret from the environment; an identity provider's are its config entry's.

signUp.description: invite (default): an admin creates accounts. open: anyone may sign up. { providers, domains }: an account is made at its first sign-in through an identity provider, with a verified email in one of the domains.

store.description: Where accounts and sessions live: a SQLite file, or a postgres:// URL (name its password, or the whole URL, by a ${NAME} reference; migratePostgresAuthStore from @mistriwork/mistri/commands makes its schema before the first start). Never a business database, which a tenant App refuses at startup. Default: a SQLite file in the mistri config directory, named for the app.

defaultRole.description: The role a new account gets. Default: user.

rows.description: Row scoping: every row (default), a server-defined row policy (needs named sources), or tenant enrollment (exactly one named source).

challenge.description: The human check every public door asks before it reads a submission: the name of a verifier the commands module exports in challenges (defineChallenges from @mistriwork/mistri/commands).

public.description: What a signed-out visitor reads: each resource named, read-only, optionally narrowed by fields; the rest of the App still needs a session. Needs roles, and rows 'all'.

roles.description: Grants within the resource ceilings. Needs at least one resources.<r>.access; omitted grants deny.

create.description: Make each new account's row the first time it is signed in to the App: its email in column (which must be unique) and, where name names a column, its name there. Every other column the row needs must have a default. Not in a tenant App yet.

me.description: Who me is as a row: the table people are rows of and its column holding their sign-in email, so owner_id = me compares a reference to that table with the signed-in person's row. Without it, me is the account's email and compares with text columns only. In a tenant App column holds the account's id, and me is the row of the tenant the request is in; a tenant with no row for them matches nothing.

tenancy.description: What one tenant is called, the platform-owned profile resource with one row per tenant, and the platform realm with its label. Only with auth.rows 'tenant'.

label.description: What one tenant is called in the chooser and the browser's own words ("Dealer").

profile.description: The platform-owned resource with one row per tenant. A tenant's row may reference it, only through its ownership column.

platform.description: Declares the platform realm, the business above the tenants. The server-only policy must then declare resolvePlatformRows.

label.description: What the platform realm is called in the chooser ("Lender").

me.description: Who me is in the platform realm, as auth.me says it in a tenant's: the platform-owned resource its staff are rows of, and the column holding each one's account id, so a provider view can say owner_id = me. A tenant's member is never this row, and the platform's staff are never a tenant's person.

order.description: A numeric column holding each card's place in its lane; the lanes read in its order, and a reader who may edit it drags a card into place.

category.description: A column whose value is the card's kind: a chip over the title in the color its display rule's colors give the value, and the card's stripe where the look draws one.

footer.description: Facts along the card's foot, each a column with an optional icon; a person stands at the right end.

swimlanes.description: A column whose values are rows across the lanes, one per value plus one for none; a card changes row by an ordinary update where the reader may edit the column, and keeps its row, told why, where not.

limits.description: A lane's work-in-progress limit by lane value: its head says count / limit and warns past it. Shown, never enforced.

sum.description: A numeric column summed in each lane's head beside its count. Absent, the first money column the card shows is summed; money is said short ($240K), whole in the title.

folded.description: Lane values drawn folded until a reader opens one (a closed stage: won, lost): a narrow strip with its name, count and sum. Remembered per board in the reader's browser.

primary.description: The card's title: a text column, a reference, which says the record it names (sales_order_id titles a parcel by its order), or a one-hop label path like "patient_id.name". A reference in lines or footer says its record's name too.

boardList.description: Lanes of cards by one local column; a card moves only through an update that sets exactly that column, judged by its when, or a machine's command verb that leads there from the card's state (told the lane where its command asks for the column), run as its button runs it.

splitListDetail.description: The view's own list — its show, query, tabs and filter bar — beside one selected record, headed by the resource's noun. No hooks, persistence, or component registry.

row.description: How a row reads in the list beside the record, in the queue's vocabulary: a title, up to two lines, captioned properties, a status badge and an avatar. Absent, the list is the plain grid.

badge.description: A status said as its tone, from the column's display map.

avatar.description: A name or person drawn as an avatar of initials before the row.

oneHopName.description: A local column or a one-hop reference label path.

show.description: Columns, in order: a column or a dotted label path. Captions are the resource's labels.

splitShow.description: Columns for the split workspace: a column or a label path. Presentation only; it grants no access.

presentation.description: How the rows draw: a checklist, a queue, a calendar, cards — each a card of one primary column and its lines — or the App's own component (custom); a board or a split is the list view's own board or split key. Local readable columns only; none grants writes.

oneOf.description: A text primary, a boolean it toggles (SQLite BOOLEAN), one line beneath.

properties.description: Up to six captioned values under the title: local columns or one-hop label paths.

badge.description: An optional status cue, dressed by the column's display tones.

openLabel.description: The row-opening call to action; omitted uses Open.

oneOf.description: A keyboard-first selection queue: the resource's bulk actions apply to exactly the selected records.
Records as the tree their parent column (a local reference to the same table) makes, opened a level at a time.
Records as bars from start to end along time, a row per value of `by`, today ruled across: a Gantt chart.

date.description: The date (or timestamp) column a record sits on, or starts on when it has an end.

end.description: A date column holding the record's last day: the record is drawn across every day from date to end, continuing across week rows. A move shifts both.

primary.description: A local text column or one-hop reference label path like "employee_id.name".

badge.description: A status said as its tone (a dot and its word) from the column's display map: a local column or one-hop label path.

resource.description: The resource whose rows are the spans, like 'blackout'.

from.description: Its date (or timestamp) column where a span starts.

to.description: Its date (or timestamp) column holding a span's last day.

label.description: Its column whose value names a span.

tone.description: The span's shade, in a display tone; absent, the quiet neutral.

resource.description: The resource whose rows are the spans, like 'blackout'.

from.description: Its date (or timestamp) column where a span starts.

to.description: Its date (or timestamp) column holding a span's last day.

label.description: Its column whose value names a span.

tone.description: The span's shade, in a display tone; absent, the quiet neutral.

backdrop.description: Shaded spans behind the days, read from another resource through the reader's own grants (a blackout window): one kind or up to four, each from one date column to another, named by a label column, in a display tone. A span opens its record where its resource has a list the reader can open.

oneOf.description: A month of records by one date column, each on its day — or, with end, across the days from date to end; a phone reads it as an agenda.

primary.description: The card's title: a text column, or one a reference names ("vehicle_id.title"). Omitted, the record's name (the resource's recordLabel).

description.description: A text column said under the title at the card's full width, without a caption, clamped to three lines.

value.description: One prominent figure, the row's own or one a reference names ("vehicle_id.price"), read through that table's grants.

icon.description: A column whose display rule maps its values to icons: the card wears its value's icon before the title.

properties.description: Up to four values under the title, each under its caption: a local column or a one-hop label path ("dealer_id.name").

facts.description: Up to six values said in one line under the figure, a dot between ("2019 · 85,780 mi · Hybrid"): local columns or one-hop label paths.

oneOf.description: A fact and the word said with its value: { column: 'owners', after: 'owner' } reads "1 owner", "3 owners"; { column: 'born_on', before: 'Born' } reads "Born Apr 24, 2017".

footer.description: Up to four values along the card's foot under a hairline, written as facts are: a catalog item's price and how long it takes.

oneOf.description: A fact and the word said with its value: { column: 'owners', after: 'owner' } reads "1 owner", "3 owners"; { column: 'born_on', before: 'Born' } reads "Born Apr 24, 2017".

image.description: A text column holding an https:// or /-rooted image address (the row's own, or one a reference names), or the first file of a related file resource (with of, the referenced record's).

about.description: A reference column of the card's row: the files are the record it names.

from.description: A resource whose rows are files.

whose.description: The column of from that names the card's record.

sort.description: Which file leads: one column and an optional direction, like "position".

media.description: How the image is framed. Omit or use cover for the existing picture; avatar makes it a circular portrait and falls back to initials from primary.

oneOf.description: A responsive grid of cards: a picture, the title, one prominent figure, up to four facts and a badge; the whole card opens its record.
A list view's rows drawn by the App's own component (customList). The platform keeps the query, tabs, filters, sort, paging and bulk actions.

show.description: The columns the component reads, label paths welcome.

props.description: The component's props, checked against its declaration.

listView.description: The rows of one resource. The key is its address.

icon.description: The menu's mark for this view: in the side and top menus, and alone in the icon rail.

from.description: A logical resource name: bare, or source.name for a secondary source.

path.description: Its address after the App's (/{app}/{path}), when not its key.

query.description: Standing conditions; tabs refine on top.

segment.description: One of the table's segments (resources.<table>.segments), its conditions ANDed with query.

empty.description: Copy for an empty base list, with an optional link to another App list, dashboard or signed-in form. Tabs and filters retain the ordinary no-matches message.

tabs.description: Tabs over the rows: a segment of the table by name, a segment with its own sort, or every row ({ label }). A tab's label and address are its segment's.

oneOf.description: A segment of the list's table, by name.

sort.description: The order this tab reads in, as the query bar writes one ("scheduled_at", "created_on desc"); wins over the view's own sort.

oneOf.description: Every row, called label.

anyOf.description: The rows that point at the record: { has: 'opportunity', filter: 'stage' }, or a segment of theirs as a yes-or-no; whose names the reference where they have several.

has.description: The resource whose rows point at the list's record: opportunity.

filter.description: A column of those rows, or a path up from them, whose values the filter lists: stage, tag_id.

segment.description: One of their segments, a yes-or-no: { has: 'opportunity', segment: 'open' } is Has open opportunities.

whose.description: Their reference to the record, where they have more than one: account_id.

filters.description: Columns offered as quick filter boxes — a rollup or computed column too, a number's Min and Max (spent). A path up a reference (account_id.industry_id) filters by the record it names, and { has } by the rows that point at it. Empty means none, on purpose.

filterBar.description: Where the filters sit: bar (the default) above the rows; rail, a rail of facets beside the rows (not beside a split); none hides the filter bar, and tabs remain visible.

suggest.description: A text filter (one of filters) to the text columns whose values it suggests as the reader types, like { "title": ["make", "model"] }.

shortcuts.description: A split's single keys: a key (one lowercase letter or digit, not J or K) to the id of an action of the picked record. Each shows beside its verb, and works only while focus is not in an input.

heading.description: false draws the list without its title; it stays for a screen reader.

count.description: With ui.shell.counts: true counts this list in the menu, false never does. Absent, the list is counted where its condition is work: its machine's unfinished states, a date at or before today, or the reader (me).

advancedFilters.description: Opt in to the Advanced action and raw query editor. Hidden by default in App lists; filterBar 'none' still hides the whole bar.

quickAdd.description: Inline the resource's New form above the rows.

import.description: This list's own CSV import, or false for none where its resource offers one.

favorite.description: Opt-in: a star on the view, so a reader can keep it in Favorites.

totals.description: Numeric columns, rollups or computed numbers summed in a footer row, over everything the list's conditions match, not just the page. A grid only.

sort.description: The list's order, written like the query bar: "created_on desc" is how it reads when nothing else says one. Two to eight named orders are a Sort menu beside the filters, the first of them the order the list opens in; a chosen one is the query's own sort clause, so the address keeps it. The opening order is kept out of the bar, as order is. A tab's sort clause wins over it, and the menu over both. Not beside order or a sort in query, and not on a board or a calendar.

order.description: A numeric column holding each row's place: the list reads in its order wherever nothing else sorts it, and a reader who may edit it drags a row into place, presses Alt+↑/↓, or picks a place from the row's grip. A grid, a checklist, a queue or cards (a board's is its presentation's order); not with a sort in query.

density.description: Row height: 'comfortable' (default) or 'compact', for a list read as a ledger. A reader's zoom still applies.

rowActions.description: A ⋯ menu at the end of each row with the record's own actions, as its page offers them. A grid only.

editable.description: Cells edited in place where the reader may write the column (Enter or F2 opens, Enter saves, Esc cancels, Tab saves and moves on), and a selection's "Set field…". true offers every shown column the reader may write; a list, only those: shown local columns (a reference shown by its record's name, owner_id.name, is edited as owner_id, with a picker), never the key, a document, a file's columns or the resource's machine column. A grid only, on a resource with access 'write'.

open.description: How rows open: the full page (default), a drawer over the list, or a modal. Not beside a split, which opens its own rows.

opens.description: A reference column whose record a row opens, in place of the row itself: a list of a join table such as ticket_watcher opens the ticket each row is about (opens: 'ticket_id'). A grid only.

sizing.description: Fit available width (default), or preserve content widths with horizontal scrolling.

actions.description: Queue and board only: narrows the resource's actions by id, in order. Never defines one.

realm.description: The realm it belongs to: a tenant's (the default) or the platform realm's, which needs auth.tenancy.platform.

roles.description: The roles that may open it: a signed-in reader holding none of them is not served it (not in the menu, ⌘K or search, and its address answers as one that does not exist). Table grants still apply; this only narrows. Each must be declared in auth.roles.

dashArea.description: The area of the dashboard's areas this section is placed in. Sections in one area stack in source order.

dashSection.description: One section of a dashboard, by kind. Each kind takes exactly the keys the parser reads for it (SECTION_KEYS in packages/mistri/src/shared/app.ts).

oneOf.description: One number, with compare for a delta.

icon.description: A curated mark in the section’s heading row.

from.description: The table the section reads. Absent means the dashboard-level table.

query.description: The query language, without the leading table name.

segment.description: One of the table's segments (resources.<table>.segments), its conditions ANDed with query.

measure.description: "count" (default), "sum amount as pipeline", "median amount" (PostgreSQL only), or a computed measure: aggregates and numbers joined by + - * /, "sum won / sum amount as win_rate".

compare.description: A second query for the same measure; the card shows the delta. The phrase "previous period" derives it from the query's one "last N days/weeks/months/years" window; with no window in the query and an "over", it is the period before the window the reader picks. Unsaid on a metric with an "over", it is "previous period"; with neither an "over" nor a window in the query, "previous period" is refused.

better.description: Which way is good news, so the delta wears good/bad. Absent means neutral. Without "compare" or "over" there is no delta to color.

spark.description: Draw the measure’s monthly trend (last 12 months of "over") inside the card while no window stands; a windowed metric draws its trend across the window unless this is false. Composes with the card’s own query — best on cards whose query carries no time clause, and whose clock points backward (an opened_on, not an open deal’s close_date).

format.description: metric: how the figure is said where its measure is not one column's: percent (the figure is 0–100, said with %), number, money in the App's currency, or duration (the figure is seconds, said as "10h 2m").

unit.description: metric: a word said after the figure ("days", "/mo").

from.description: The resource the goal is read from. Absent means the metric's.

areas.description: The sections placed on a grid: one string per row, the same count of 1 to 4 space-separated cells in each, a cell an area name or . for none. aside.description: Sections in an independent context column beside the dashboard's main flow, drawn as a record page's aside: a landmark of its own, its lists drawn as names, the main flow's rows by width beside it and neither column's height waiting on the other's. windows.description: The time windows offered when any section declares "over", in the query grammar’s own words. Default: last 30 days / last 90 days / last 12 months.

window.description: The window the dashboard opens on, one of its windows ("last 30 days"); unsaid, it opens on all time. An address's ?period= still wins, and a reader's All time is said ?period=all-time.

windowControl.description: How the windows are offered: segmented (default), a button each; button, one button saying the dates covered, opening a menu of the windows.

filters.description: Pick-filters: column names offered as selectors in the control row. A pick narrows every section whose table has the column; a vocabulary column offers its values, a whole single-column reference offers the records it points at, by name.

favorite.description: Opt-in: a star on the view, so a reader can keep it in Favorites.

badge.description: A few words in a chip over the heading, with an App icon where it names one.

tiles.description: Two to four photos as tiles beside the words, in place of image: each a row of a file resource that auth.public reads.

points.description: Up to four icon rows under the actions, each an App icon and a short line. Not with highlights.

icon.description: The menu's mark for a signed-in form. A public form is in no menu and takes none.

path.description: A signed-in form's address after the App's, when not its key. A public form is /{app}/form/{key}.

steps.description: Every command input is asked on exactly one step. Without steps the form is one page. A step that names its own command instead of fields makes the form one saved on every step; then every step names one.

style.description: How the steps are drawn, both under one progress bar: the stepper (default, the step's name over its fields) or the intake style (one question at a time, a sticky bar of actions and an editable review).

note.description: Intake: a quiet line over the progress bar.

review.description: Intake: whether the last page reviews every answer (default true).

done.description: The screen after a submission, beside the reference the handler returned when it returned one.

public.description: Served signed out at /{app}/form/{key} under the public rules: a public command, its pickers over what `auth.public` reads, never in nav. Absent means signed in.

prefillable.description: The command's inputs a link's address may start filled (?stock_ref=FC-1049): text, number, date or choice inputs, shown, editable and checked like anything typed. A form that names none fills none.

resume.description: The root row's columns the platform keeps: the SHA-256 of the applicant's cookie, the expiry and the saved steps' ids. Nullable text, a timestamp, nullable text.

after.description: How long from the first step a draft may be resumed: '14 days' or '2 weeks' (the default is 14 days), a whole number of days, 1 to 90.

draft.description: The one root column and the value an unfinished application holds until submit: { status: 'in_progress' }. Staff lists hide it by default.

abandoned.description: An expired draft: 'purge' (the default) removes the root and the rows that point at it; 'keep' leaves them for follow-up.

statusCheck.description: The one sanctioned read of an anonymous application: the random receipt confirmed by one to three values only the applicant knows. Answers a state, never an input.

stepUp.description: More after a one-time code to the root's email column, sent by the config's email service: the check's details again with the code, then its show columns for a short session.

alert.description: A nullable timestamp column stamped when a submitted application's receipt locks; a notify rule on the root watching it tells staff.

link.description: Adding a submitted application to an account on proven control: sameDevice (the browser's 30-minute claim, spent by a signed-in Yes), statusCheck (a signed-in status check) and/or email (an account's verified email offers the applications that captured it, each added by a Yes). email.description: The root's email column (a step's input), or { column, verified }: verified is the text column the server stamps with the address the applicant proved with a code in the form, which links without asking.

roles.description: A signed-in form's: the roles that may open it, within those granted its command. Never on a public form. Each must be declared in auth.roles.

inputs.description: A form's input drawn by the App's own input component (kind 'input'), a public form's too, whose page loads it. An input in a group is named by its path (trade.vin), and in a repeating group stands in every row.

formView.description: A command form: one form running one command that creates records. Signed in unless it says public: true, when it is served signed out at /{app}/form/{key}.

view.description: Everything a visitor can open, by kind.

inline.description: In the top bar, a top-level group's entries stand in the bar as links of their own, not under its menu. The sidebar still draws the group.

folded.description: In the sidebar, the section starts folded to its heading for someone who has never opened or closed it. Their own fold is remembered over it; it still opens while it holds the current room, while filtering, and in the rail.

navPlacement.description: In the App's nav and its groups only: the named feature's nav fragment, spliced in place. Each fragment is placed once.

navColor.description: A dot in the entry's icon place, in one of the theme's eight chart colors (1-8).

navNode.description: A local view id, a { label, to } naming a view, a static checked { label, to } link, a group, or in the App's nav a { feature } placement. Never a definition.

logoFile.description: A PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF or SVG file, by its path in the App's directory.

recordBranding.description: Server-bound record branding. The authorized reader selects a row; stored data never supplies CSS or a URL.

ui.description: Chrome and formatting: the one nested block of the root.

footer.description: The App's footer, drawn under every room.

src.description: The picture the bar draws, in a 96 by 24 box.

dark.description: The picture drawn on a dark bar: in dark mode, and by day under a theme whose bar is dark.

mark.description: A square picture for the browser tab; omitted, the tab shows src.

shell.description: App shell visibility, spacing and placement. Omitted settings keep the existing UI.

editing.description: Existing-record save preference. Omission keeps explicit Save; Workbench always uses explicit review/apply. Grants no write capability.

export.description: false hides the Export menu everywhere the app curates, and the server refuses the file as well, over any role's export grant. Default true.

locale.description: BCP 47 tag the App is said and written in: the language of its captions where it has messages/ catalogs, and every figure — numbers, money, percents, dates, times, relative days and counts ("en-AU"). Absent: the reader’s browser decides the figures. { column, default } reads each reader's own tag from the first row of that text column they may read; a tenant's (branding allow locale) comes next, then default.

column.description: The resource's text column naming the reader's language tag: "person.locale".

default.description: The App's own language: its source catalog's, and the reader's where nothing nearer names one.

messages.description: A tenant's own words over the App's catalogs, read from a record: fromRecord(resource, { by: 'tenant', tenantField, fields: { key, locale, text } }). A row is checked as it is written — a key the source catalog has, a language tag, ICU text reading only the source's arguments — and a row that fails is skipped when read.

timezone.description: IANA zone the app’s "today" is reckoned in ("Australia/Sydney"). Absent: the server’s clock. A TIMESTAMP or DATETIME that carries no zone holds the wall clock in this zone (UTC when the App names none) — whatever writes it: an action's now, a machine's since, a Date a command writes, a New form's now. A column with a zone (timestamptz) holds the instant. { column, default } counts each reader's days in the zone the first row of that text column they may read names (their tenant's, their account's); writes keep default.

column.description: The resource's text column naming the reader's IANA zone: "desk_setting.timezone".

default.description: The App's own zone: what writes keep, and the reader's where the row names none.

currency.description: ISO 4217 default for money rules that name none. Defaults to USD.

csp.description: The origins the page opens beside the App's own for its custom components, recorded in authority.lock.

connect.description: Origins its custom components may send requests to (https://api.example.com): the page's connect-src.

images.description: Origins its custom components may load pictures from, beside its own: the page's img-src. Once an App serves components, pictures come only from its own origin and these.

feature.description: A slice of an App's content. The App keeps its identity, sources, sign-in, roles and ui.

id.description: Unique in the App. Names the feature in refusals, the authority report and a nav placement; never part of an address.

resources.description: How resources present and what can be done to them. A binding or ceiling here restates the App's own exactly.

roles.description: Grants to roles the App declares in auth.roles; a feature never creates a role.

views.description: Everything a visitor can open, keyed: the key is the view’s address.

pages.description: Record pages keyed by id, or one file per page under pages/ (its basename the key).

nav.description: This feature's own views, arranged. The App's nav places it with { feature: '<id>' }; without an App nav, the fragments are the menu, in features order.

home.description: Rules appended after the App's, in features order. None may follow a rule that already matches every visitor.

appFooter.description: A line of small print and a row of links. Under ui it is drawn beneath every room of the App; a landing with none of its own wears it.

componentProp.description: A prop a component declares: prop.number(), prop.text(), prop.bool() or prop.choice([...]); JSON-safe, checked where it is placed.

component.description: An author's own React module, referenced by path — component('id', { module }) — and placed through a declared kind: a custom section, a value renderer where a display rule stands, an input where a form draws a field, a list view's rows (customList) or a free-form page (definePage, in pages/<path>.page.tsx).

module.description: A path inside the App directory, written from it: './widgets/Thing.tsx'.

kind.description: section (default): a custom section. value: a value renderer. input: a form field's control. list: a list view's rows. A free-form page is a file of its own (pages/<path>.page.tsx, definePage), not a component.

commandName.description: A command, by its name in the App's commands module (defineCommands). The server fills in its input, target and version from the registration; mistri-commands.d.ts types the names.

machine.description: The record's states and the verbs that move it between them, in the record's order. A verb that names one of the App's commands runs it; any other word is a fixed move that sets the column. The column changes only along the graph, on every door.

since.description: A timestamp column the server stamps when the state changes; `after` timers count from it.

entry.description: The states a command may insert a new record in besides the first, such as a converted lead's deal opening past qualification. A form's New record still starts in the first state.

groups.description: Named sets of states the query language reads as it reads `status is open`: `status is onBench` means the group's states, `status is not onBench` the others. A group is never named like a state, nor `open`, which `status is open` says (every state that is not final).

label.description: The button's words; {to} says the state it leads to. A command verb may say itself differently from different states.

confirm.description: Ask before the move writes. A command verb that asks nothing asks first too; one with inputs asks them in its form, which is its confirmation, and is refused one.

after.description: How long the record may stay, and the command run through the jobs then.

by.description: Moves only a service role makes (auth.roles.<role>.service): the states a command running as it may move the record to. Drawn as no button.
